# Independent registration checker/reference controls

These are unchanged-original source observations, not native registration output.
The private capture ran all 119 ordinary cases, 12 hardware cases and three real
wall-clock cases through the original Params bridge, signed loopback HTTP and
original collector. Four additional arbitrary-input controls exercise dynamic
query/retry/persist/value behavior. Sixteen original CLI/failure controls retain
source-before-candidate and exclusive-output phases.

`manifest.json` separately binds the 46 source inputs recorded by the original
captures, one additional original messaging input verified by a fresh pinned
Cython import, their 47-input required union, exact dependency versions, capture
receipts/scripts and every maintained corpus. The added messaging source is not
misrepresented as a field of the earlier 134-case receipt. `inputs-original.json` represents
Python bytes as `{ "bytes_hex": "..." }`; it contains no generated private keys.
`source-original.json` retains the first, extended-provider capture with complete
semantic outcomes/types/traces/Params,
normalized logs and verified requests. The sole request substitution is the
freshly generated public-key text, replaced *after* original cryptographic
signature/claims/public-key verification. Measured elapsed/shutdown durations
stay private; declared minimum durations and collector SIGINT status stay exact.
Original raw keys, tokens, cereal, Swaglog and timing receipts remain private.

The new public CLI intentionally removes the Python binding positional:
`check-registration BINARY OUTPUT [--runner RUNNER] [--case CASE] [--timeouts]
[--hardware]`. Native worker/probe prerequisites are mandatory environment paths,
never optional skips. Tests independently decode actual full cereal packets and
read actual disk files, in addition to checking original semantic expectations.
The immutable shell runner is only a process-boundary fixture: it executes the
real probe, then holds its return to permit executable/source substitution tests.
No canned probe response or production shell execution is introduced.

The native delayed-collector control uses a real Unix R/1/1 handshake and an
800ms pause after actual subscribers exist. Quiescent original-ABI queue-header
snapshots prove that the actual publisher reset invalidates those readers, and
that the debug readiness barrier refreshes the error reader before the unchanged
year-10000 error workload. This stage replaces the old Python-specific preload
seam; its native regression passed the first actual reference gate.

Native receipt contracts preserve exclusive directory admission (including any
foreign receipt), remove cancelled publication only after owning the output, and
validate bounded before/after executable/source identities. These do not claim an atomic
snapshot against adversarial ABA replacement. They do not change the captured
original policy expectations.

The declared Python3.12 CI dependency context has Requests2.34.2, urllib32.7.0,
Brotli1.2.0 and zstandard0.25.0, without optional `backports.zstd`. The shared
read-only capture environment additionally has backports.zstd1.8.0: urllib3
imports that separate provider and advertises zstd. The original checker and the
same real candidate fail with that extra header, and pass when a private import
control removes only the optional provider. Neither Requests nor original source
was edited; no package was installed or removed. The native source advertises
only its implemented gzip/deflate/Brotli capabilities, matching declared CI.
Optional zstd negotiation/decoding is explicitly outside this native context.

`source-baseline-original.json` is a **new independent unchanged-original run**:
all134 original cases plus four generic controls, not a rewritten header golden.
`provider-baseline.json` seals both contexts and their private receipts/scripts.
Across138 rows,34 have no requests and are identical;104 differ only in the
explicitly checked header (174 actual requests). Every other semantic field is
exact. Tests retain and hash both corpora, require the baseline provider context,
and compare actual full headers exactly. No allowlist or header-normalizing
comparison is used. Original `source-original.json` bytes remain unchanged.

The HTTP text boundary additionally retains150 unchanged Requests.Response.text
observations covering every captured response body. The actual full reference
loop exposed the missing legacy UTF-8 BOM-to-`utf_8_sig` rename at case67; the
adapter now makes that rename only during automatic detection. Three separately
captured and actually reproduced native header regressions retain MIME case,
last duplicate charset and quoted parameter-key behavior. These153 text controls
and the unchanged original unsigned repeated-algorithm query control pass two
focused native unit tests. Verified token algorithm fields remain scalar; an
ordinary unsigned query named algorithm remains a list. No prior corpus changed.

The later full original comparison caught a second independent boundary defect:
CP949 response bytes were not encoded by the convenience encoder, so both native
sides agreed on the same incorrect fallback. The immutable original expectation
rejected that agreement. The source now uses canonical CP949 encoding derived
from the existing decoder table, checked against all 17,176 original scalar
encodings. The encoder controls also bind all 144 original non-raw response-body
scenarios, three strict rejection cases and 265 original UTF-7 controls. These
are byte comparisons, not token/result normalizations.

**Verified current boundary:** four focused codec/query units and strict Clippy
passed; the frozen integration executables passed controller8/reference5. A fresh
native-only paired run passed all131 ordinary/hardware and three real timing
cases, then independently matched the unchanged original baseline on both sides
(all268 complete typed semantic observations), including persisted disk records.
Its execve/execveat trace contains940 execution attempts and zero Python/PyPy/.py
execution. Seventeen actual CLI/failure/gated controls passed. Explicit owned,
shared-mechanic, original-input and ELF identities were checked after completion.
The private proof index is `registration-current-proof.json` under the dated
registration scratch directory; it records the exact four frozen ELF hashes.

The later combined navd/registration boundary uses nine freshly frozen ELFs and
passes registration14, navd10 and exact-retirement3 integration tests plus seven
focused units. The original13-test result above remains historical. A fresh full
134-case trace independently matches all268 original typed semantic observations,
actual signed HTTP requests and persisted collector records, again with940 exec
attempts and zero Python execution. Seventeen fresh actual CLI controls pass;
the additional permanent CLI test proves both delayed collector reset/reader
refresh schedules through the real command rather than an external Python check.

All four helpers were removed after reviewed same-nine-ELF before/after proof.
Each phase independently matches all 268 observations across 134 cases;
registration result aggregates are byte-identical and provenance changes only
by removal of the two live registration hashes (navd removes four), retaining
unchanged separate historical maps. Only those exact names may be absent (registration2,
navd4); present drift/dangling/nonregular entries reject, every other source pin
is mandatory, and live provenance excludes absent inputs while compiled historical
hashes remain separate. No old Python implementation is renamed into a maintained
fixture. The original capture manifests continue to describe the all-present
capture context without modification. The declared provider baseline and bounded
worker deadlines remain explicit limits, not universal Python/Requests claims.
